results.title: Upstage's Solar Pro 4 becomes available to civil servants on gov't network
results.content: Korean artificial intelligence (AI) startup Upstage said Tuesday that its large language model Solar Pro 4 is now fully available on the government’s shared AI platform. Civil servants can now use a domestically developed AI model for daily work inside the government’s closed administrative network. The Ministry of the Interior and Safety and the Ministry of Science and ICT run the platform. Through it, they provide AI models, data and development tools to central government agencies and local governments. Solar Pro 4 is offered through FabriX, an AI agent platform from Samsung SDS, the IT services affiliate of Samsung Group. The model runs on network infrastructure that passed a security review by the National Intelligence Service, Korea’s spy agency. Internal government data remains within the network. results.title: Korean crypto exchanges on alert after $6.3 billion Binance hack
results.content: Korea’s cryptocurrency industry is on alert following a $6.3 billion hack at Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange. As signs emerge that the stolen assets are being laundered, domestic exchanges are seeking regulatory changes that would allow them to promptly halt withdrawals following hacks at other platforms, financial authorities and industry officials said Tuesday. The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) attributed the theft to North Korea in a statement released Saturday, saying the attackers stole about $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance on Thursday. Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis said the North Korean hackers appeared to have entered a second stage of laundering the proceeds. results.title: CJ ONE offers grocery coupons, convenience store discounts in November promotion
results.content: CJ ONE, a lifestyle membership program run by CJ OliveNetworks, is holding its November Wonder Week promotion with discounts at CJ CheilJedang’s online mall and the convenience store chain emart24, the company said Tuesday. CJ ONE is the loyalty program of CJ Group, one of Korea’s largest conglomerates. Members earn and spend points across the group’s businesses and its partner brands. The promotion runs until Nov. 10. It offers coupons for CJ The Market, the official online store of food giant CJ CheilJedang, and is tied to the store’s monthly sale event. Members who sign up in the CJ ONE app by Thursday for a notice that the promotion has opened will get a random reward. It is either a CJ The Market credit coupon worth 1,000 won, 3,000 won or 10,000 won, or CJ ONE points. results.title: SK Telecom named UN Global Compact LEAD company for 2027
results.content: SK Telecom has been named a 2027 LEAD company by the UN Global Compact (UNGC) Network Korea in recognition of its sustainability leadership, the mobile carrier said Tuesday. The company received the designation at the 2026 Korea Leaders Summit, which the network hosted at Grand Hyatt Seoul. The UN Global Compact is the world’s largest corporate sustainability initiative, launched by the United Nations in 2000. It encourages companies to build principles on human rights, labor, the environment and anti-corruption into their operations. Each year, the Korean network chooses about 10 companies and institutions as LEAD participants from its roughly 360 members. The selections recognize contributions to spreading sustainability management and developing the country’s ESG ecosystem. results.title: Kim Ha-seong not tendered qualifying offer by Braves
results.content: Korean infielder Kim Ha-seong has not received a qualifying offer from the Atlanta Braves after an injury-plagued season. Eight players received the one-year qualifying offer worth $23.15 million, the mean salary of the 125 highest-paid players in Major League Baseball (MLB), on Monday (U.S. local time). Kim played this season on a one-year, $20 million deal but batted just .116 with zero home runs and nine RBIs in 51 games. He missed the early part of the season after suffering a finger injury in January while in Korea — he slipped on ice and fell, tearing a tendon in his right middle finger — and never found his rhythm at the plate. He made his season debut on May 12 but then missed about a month, from early July to early August, with inflammation in his surgically repaired finger. He batted just 1-for-28 in June. results.title: North Korea's crypto heists threaten global security
results.content: North Korea’s record-breaking $6.3 billion cryptocurrency heist targeting Binance poses a serious threat to global security. Since the 2010s, state-sponsored hackers have carried out malicious cyberattacks, generating illicit revenue to finance the country’s missile and nuclear programs. The Binance heist should serve as a wake-up call to the international community, highlighting the need to take North Korea’s digital asset theft seriously and develop coordinated countermeasures. The latest cryptocurrency heist has raised the alarm in South Korea. Concerned that it could be North Korea’s next target, Seoul is scrambling to strengthen its cybersecurity infrastructure against attacks by state-sponsored hackers. results.title: Journey to Gongju, the ancient capital of Ungjin
results.content: On a drizzly Saturday in October, we left Seoul at 8 a.m. aboard a luxury limousine bus provided by the Seoul JoongAng Rotary Club for its annual autumn outing. Our first destination in Gongju, the ancient capital of Baekje, was Magok Temple, founded in 640. A UNESCO World Heritage site, the temple exudes a quiet grandeur. Its weathered wooden buildings with faded traditional decorative patterns and graceful tiled roofs reflect centuries of Buddhist devotion. A clear stream winds through the surrounding mountains, while peaceful forest trails invite quiet reflection. The temple stay program made me imagine spending a peaceful night here, away from modern distractions. Magok Temple also preserves a chapter of modern Korean history. results.title: Dongwha Electrolyte joins $95 mil. next-generation battery research initiative
results.content: Dongwha Electrolyte is joining a major national research initiative to develop sodium-ion batteries, as Korea seeks to advance alternatives to lithium-based energy storage and strengthen its position in the next generation of battery technology. The company, an affiliate of Dongwha Enterprise, said Tuesday that it would participate in the Market-Leading Next-Generation Secondary Battery Innovation Strategic Research Group, known as K-BIC, under the government's Global TOP Strategic Research Group support program. The initiative has a total budget of 130 billion won ($95 million) and brings together major players from industry, academia, research institutions and government to overcome technical barriers, secure foundational technologies and build a collaborative research platform. results.title: Korean Air requires Ebola declarations for all US-bound passengers
results.content: Korean Air will require all passengers traveling to the United States to submit an Ebola-related declaration confirming they have not visited or stayed in the Democratic Republic of the Congo within the previous 21 days, as part of new U.S. health measures. The airline said Monday the requirement will take effect for flights departing at or after 1:59 p.m. Wednesday, following an administrative order issued by the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to prevent the spread of Ebola from the Democratic Republic of Congo. The measure applies to all U.S.-bound routes and covers U.S. citizens, residents, airline crew members, visitors and passengers transiting through the United States en route to other countries. results.title: Wave of cyber breaches exposes growing risks to Korea's digital economy
results.content: A relentless wave of cyberattacks on Korean banks, telecom operators, businesses and government agencies has exposed growing risks to the country's digital economy, highlighting the need for stronger cybersecurity. The scale and frequency of the breaches have raised concerns that cyber threats could extend beyond personal data theft to disrupt financial services, business operations and industrial supply chains. The latest series of security breaches has brought those concerns to the highest levels of government. Most recently, police have launched a preliminary investigation into the online leak of personal information belonging to 168 individuals who traveled aboard the presidential aircraft during a trip to Europe in June, including President Lee Jae Myung, the first lady and Cabinet ministers. results.title: NIS asks 2,100 public institutions to conduct emergency cybersecurity checks
results.content: Korea's spy agency has asked 2,100 public institutions to conduct emergency cybersecurity inspections following a series of cyberattacks on financial firms that resulted in customer data breaches, government sources said Tuesday. The National Intelligence Service (NIS) has called on the central government agencies and local governments to carry out their own security checks based on a checklist, the sources said. Separately, the NIS plans to conduct its own vulnerability assessments of critical information and communications infrastructure in the public sector under its jurisdiction, the sources said. The assessments are expected to be completed by mid-November. results.title: Congolese diaspora elects new leadership in Korea
results.content: Congolese professionals and academics in Korea have elected a new leadership team, seeking to strengthen ties within their diaspora community and expand cooperation with Korean institutions. The Dynamic of the Congolese Elite in Korea, known in French as Dynamique de l'Élite Congolaise en Corée du Sud, held an extraordinary and elective general assembly, bringing together members of the Congolese academic and professional community. The meeting opened under the leadership of Eloi Fataki, vice president of the General Assembly, followed by a presentation by professor Merlec Mpyana, who reviewed the organization's history and its mission to unite and empower Congolese intellectuals and professionals in Korea. results.title: Exhibition honors German journalist who documented Gwangju Massacre
results.content: A special exhibition honoring the late German journalist Jürgen Hinzpeter (1937-2016) will open in Gwangju on Thursday, marking the 10th anniversary of his passing. Titled "Records Live On — The Blue-Eyed Witness, Hinzpeter's Legacy," the exhibition will run through March 28, 2027, at the former South Jeolla Provincial Office. The event is co-hosted by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism's Restoration Project Team and the May 18 Memorial Foundation. Hinzpeter is widely remembered in Korea and abroad as the real-life foreign correspondent portrayed in the hit 2017 feature film "A Taxi Driver." In May 1980, Korea's military dictatorship unleashed a violent crackdown on pro-democracy demonstrators in the southwestern city — an uprising now remembered as the Gwangju Massacre. results.title: 'Omniscient Reader,' 9 other works win main prizes at World Webtoon Awards
results.content: Ten Korean webtoons, including “Omniscient Reader” and “Return of the Mount Hua Sect,” have won main prizes at this year’s World Webtoon Awards, the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism said Tuesday. Webtoons are digital comics made to be read by scrolling down on a smartphone. The format began in Korea in the early 2000s and has since spread around the world. The other winners are “The S-Classes That I Raised,” “Debut or Die,” “The Greatest Estate Developer,” “Cry, or Better Yet, Beg,” “Killer Pietro,” “Real Man,” “Jakdu” and “On the Way to Meet Mom.” Each winner will receive a trophy and 10 million won ($7,500). The ministry and the Korea Creative Content Agency, a state-run body that promotes Korea’s cultural content industries, launched the awards in 2024. results.title: Lee set for summit with Turkey's Erdogan to discuss deepening cooperation
results.content: President Lee Jae Myung was set to hold a summit with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan on Tuesday to discuss ways to deepen cooperation between their countries, as well as security issues. Erdogan arrived in South Korea on Monday for a three-day state visit, marking his first trip to the country since 2018. Lee and the Turkish leader last met in Ankara in July on the occasion of a North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) summit hosted by Turkey. Tuesday's summit is expected to explore ways to boost bilateral cooperation in various sectors, including trade, investment, the defense industry, nuclear power plants and other future industries. The leaders are also expected to exchange views on the situations on the Korean Peninsula and in the Middle East, Seoul's presidential office said earlier. results.title: Korea launches 3,600-ton submarine, boosting naval deterrence, defense export capacity
results.content: Korea’s Navy and Defense Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA) launched the Seo Hui (SS-088), the nation’s second 3,600-ton Dosan Ahn Changho-class Batch-II diesel-electric attack submarine, during a ceremony at Hanwha Ocean’s Geoje Okpo Shipyard on Tuesday. The vessel is named after Seo Hui (942–998), a prominent diplomat and statesman of the Goryeo Dynasty renowned for using strategic negotiation to fend off a massive invasion by the Khitan-led Liao Empire in 993, securing vital territory along the northwestern border without shedding blood. Navigating regional security threats around the peninsula, Korea designated his name to symbolize military foresight, national crisis resolution and maritime sovereignty defense. results.title: 9 Korean picture books win national award, set sights on global readers
results.content: Nine Korean picture books have been selected for the 2026 Korea Picture Book Award, with the government pledging export support to help winning authors reach readers worldwide. The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism said Tuesday that nine works were chosen from 506 entries for the fourth annual awards, established in 2023 to promote the development of Korean picture books and expand their presence in overseas markets. The awards ceremony is scheduled for 2 p.m. Tuesday at Ferrum Tower in central Seoul. The two grand prizes went to Jeon Mi-hwa's "To the Fish in the Sea, to the Birds in the Sky, to the Animals in the Forest, and to Humans" in fiction and Kim Ji-won's "Raising Earthworms" in nonfiction. results.title: T.O.P, Nana make surprise appearance at fan-organized birthday cafe
results.content: T.O.P and Nana have made an unexpected appearance together at a fan-organized birthday cafe, just one day after the former BIGBANG member apologized to longtime supporters following the closure of a fansite that had backed him for nearly 20 years. A video showing the couple visiting the cafe in Seoul's Gangnam District was posted Monday on the venue's social media account. The cafe was decorated by fans to celebrate T.O.P's birthday on Wednesday. The appearance drew particular attention as T.O.P and Nana publicly confirmed their relationship only last month. In the video, T.O.P, whose real name is Choi Seung-hyun, wears a black jacket, white mask and cap as he looks around the fan-decorated space. results.title: Sales of Galaxy Z Fold 8 increase following launch of Apple's 1st foldable smartphone
results.content: Domestic sales of Samsung Electronics Co.'s latest Galaxy Z foldable smartphone have increased following the launch of Apple Inc.'s first foldable iPhone, industry sources said Tuesday. Sales of the Galaxy Z Fold 8 in Korea rose about 20 percent in the week after the iPhone Duo's launch from the previous week, according to telecommunications industry sources. The increase is believed to reflect consumer recognition of Samsung's hinge technology and product durability, as well as the user experience offered by its artificial intelligence (AI) features, they said. The Galaxy Z8 series previously set a record for presales of Samsung smartphones in Korea, with 1.44 million units sold during its presale period in July.

results.title: Korea, Bulgaria reaffirm economic ties, nuclear cooperation
results.content: Korea and Bulgaria have reaffirmed their commitment to cooperation on a new nuclear power plant project in Bulgaria and discussed ways to expand bilateral economic ties at a joint committee meeting, Seoul's foreign ministry said Tuesday. The third meeting of the Korea-Bulgaria Joint Economic Committee was held in Sofia on Monday (local time), co-chaired by Park Jong-han, deputy minister for economic affairs, and Krasimir Yakimov, the Bulgarian deputy economic minister, according to the ministry. The meeting marked the first gathering of the committee in seven years, following the previous session in Seoul in September 2019. The inaugural meeting was held in Sofia in September 2015. results.title: N. Korea slams Japan's missile reinforcement, joint drills with US
results.content: North Korea on Tuesday criticized Japan's push to acquire "preemptive attack" capabilities and last month's regular military drills between Washington and Tokyo, warning that such moves would invite a "vicious cycle" of escalating regional tensions. In an article carried by the official Korean Central News Agency, a military commentator took issue with Tokyo's deployment of a Type 25 longer-range anti-ship missile launcher during the bilateral Keen Sword exercise that took place across Japan from Oct. 19-29. The Type 25 missile system with a range of more than 1,000 kilometers is part of Tokyo's efforts to bolster its "counterstrike" capabilities against potential enemy attacks. results.title: [TEST DRIVE] BYD Sealion 6 DM-i excels in quietness, range
results.content: Starting BYD Korea's Sealion 6 DM-i plug-in hybrid SUV, the first thing that stood out was the exceptional quietness of its cabin. Driving through city streets and along highways, the SUV felt more like a mid-size luxury sedan than a family-oriented SUV. In the name Sealion 6 DM-i, DM-i stands for “Dual Mode-intelligent,” BYD’s proprietary plug-in hybrid electric vehicle (PHEV) technology, which powers the vehicle's long-range drive. Its cabin remained remarkably quiet at low speeds, when the electric motor does most of the work. Minor vibrations were barely noticeable, while the suspension softened the impact of speed bumps and uneven pavement. The result was a relaxed, composed ride that made long-distance driving less tiring. results.title: Police release identity of suspect in Seoul building arson
results.content: Police on Tuesday released the identity and mug shots of a suspect accused of setting fires at two patent firms in southern Seoul last month and leaving 26 people injured. The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency posted the photos of Lee Myung-soo, 77, on its website following a decision by a review committee. Lee is suspected of committing arson in two buildings in Seoul's southern ward of Gangnam on Oct. 20, He was taken into custody shortly after the fires and was referred to the prosecution last week on charges of arson and attempted murder. Investigators believe the suspect planned the arson and was likely aware of people inside the offices. Lee has claimed that he was scammed by the patent firms and only wanted to scare people, not hurt them. results.title: Foreigners' card spending in Seoul jumps nearly 58% to $6.57 bil.
results.content: Foreign visitors' card spending in Seoul jumped nearly 58 percent from a year earlier in the first nine months of 2026, driven by a record number of visitors, city government data showed Tuesday. Foreigners spent 8.84 trillion won ($6.57 billion) using credit and debit cards in Seoul from January to September, up 57.7 percent from the same period last year, according to the data. The figure has already surpassed the annual total of 7.94 trillion won for 2025. By sector, shopping accounted for the largest share at 46 percent, followed by medical and wellness services at 23.8 percent. Food and beverages took up 13.3 percent, while accommodation accounted for 10.4 percent. By district, Gangnam Ward led spending with 29.6 percent of the total, followed by Jung Ward at 27.7 percent and Mapo Ward at 7.1 percent. results.title: Seoul shares down over 2% late Tuesday morning on AI concerns
results.content: Korean stocks traded more than 2 percent lower late Tuesday morning, led by tech losses amid lingering woes about the excessive pace of artificial intelligence (AI) spending. Opening 2.46 percent lower, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) fell 145.02 points, or 2.48 percent, to 5,714.06 as of 11:20 a.m. Overnight on Wall Street, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite and the S&P 500 closed 1.07 percent and 0.51 percent lower, respectively, ahead of the U.S. midterm elections slated for Tuesday. Investor sentiment was dampened by concerns that massive spending on AI infrastructure is undermining tech firms' near-term profitability. In Seoul, tech shares led the decline. Market bellwether Samsung Electronics sank 2.95 percent, and its chipmaking rival SK hynix slid 3.8 percent. results.title: BTS concerts in Taiwan, Indonesia to be screened at movie theaters in over 80 countries
results.content: Two shows from K-pop supergroup BTS' upcoming tour in Taiwan and Jakarta will be livestreamed at movie theaters in more than 80 countries and regions, the group's agency said Tuesday. The live viewings will feature the group's second-day show in Kaohsiung, Taiwan, on Nov. 21 and its third-day show in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Dec. 29, BigHit Music said in a notice posted on K-pop fan community platform Weverse. The Kaohsiung and Jakarta concerts will be shown on about 3,300 and 2,800 large screens worldwide, respectively. In South Korea, audiences can watch them at three major cinema chains — CGV, Lotte Cinema and Megabox. BigHit Music said screening times will be adjusted for different time zones, meaning viewers in some regions will watch delayed broadcasts one to two days later. results.title: Consumer prices up 2.8% in October, remain in 2% range for 2nd month
results.content: Korea's consumer prices rose 2.8 percent in October from a year earlier, data showed Tuesday, as agricultural product prices continued to decline despite energy costs remaining elevated. According to data from the Ministry of Data and Statistics, consumer price growth eased to 2.8 percent in October from 2.9 percent in September and 3.1 percent in August. The data ministry said petroleum products' prices advanced 14.9 percent year-on-year in October, contributing 0.56 percentage point to the month's year-on-year inflation rate. It was the sharpest growth since 15.5 percent posted in July. In detail, diesel prices jumped 19.7 percent year-on-year in October, while gasoline prices increased a sharp 11.6 percent. results.title: Glass Lewis supports Lee Jae-keun's appointment as KB Financial chairman
results.content: Glass Lewis has advised shareholders to support the appointment of Lee Jae-keun as chairman of KB Financial Group, according to a voting recommendations report exclusively obtained by The Korea Times on Tuesday. The world’s second-largest proxy advisory firm said it had identified “no substantial issues for shareholder concern” regarding the proposed appointment. The report also flagged several ongoing issues facing the group, including allegations of collusion over loan terms and subsequent investigations by the Fair Trade Commission, as well as the Financial Supervisory Service’s investigation into the potential mis-selling of Hong Kong-linked equity-linked securities.
